title: Resolve runtime symbol conflicts by introducing linker namespace isolation and staged rollout
creator: Riley Chen
description:
Problem: In a subset of customer and internal canary fleets we observe intermittent ODR-like behavior and symbol resolution collisions when loading mixed CUTLASS+CUDNN+Triton plugin stacks at runtime. The immediate symptom is segfaults during model init or degraded perf due to unexpected kernel implementations being bound. Root cause analysis indicates our current dlopen strategy uses global symbol tables (RTLD_GLOBAL) and we load multiple binary-provided shared objects with overlapping exported symbols (eg. cutlass stubs, third-party kernels). This is exacerbated during rolling upgrades where older agent processes and new runtime bundles coexist on the same host.

Goals: 1) Prevent accidental symbol hijacking by isolating third-party shared objects into linker namespaces or by using RTLD_LOCAL semantics where safe. 2) Preserve existing backwards compatibility: older model bundles should still start, and we must be able to fall back to the legacy loading path. 3) Provide deterministic kernel selection observable in traces/telemetry. 4) Stage rollout with canaries and automated rollback thresholds.

Success criteria: - No symbol-collision crashes in canary fleet for 48h after rollout. - End-to-end latency tail (p95/p99) does not regress >5% on canaries. - Deployment tooling supports per-host toggle of new loader. - Automated tests (integration+stress) exercise mixed-version stacks and cover common failure modes.

Technical approach (high level):
- Introduce a loader module that initially uses RTLD_LOCAL for all plugin dlopen calls and only exposes explicitly-registered symbols via a controlled shim (symbol registrar). On platforms that support GNU namespace (dlmopen), create a namespace per plugin bundle to fully isolate symbols. Fall back to RTLD_LOCAL on platforms without dlmopen.
- Add an opt-in compatibility shim that allows selecting a legacy-global mode for specific bundles (useful for third-party vendor libs that require global symbol visibility). This is enabled only via runtime-config and guarded with feature flags.
- Implement a prelink verification step during bundle installation that scans exported symbols and emits warnings for collisions. For high-risk collisions (e.g., symbol names matching our internal kernel stubs), fail the install and require a signed override.
- Add a kernel-binding verifier that logs the selected kernel implementation (symbol name and originating SO) to our tracing pipeline so failures are attributable to a concrete artifact.

Planned subtasks:
- Loader refactor: encapsulate all dlopen calls and add namespace/RTLD_LOCAL switching (owner: Asha)
- Installer checks: symbol scanner and policy (owner: Marco Ruiz)
- Telemetry: kernel-binding events and dashboard (owner: Priya Nair)
- CI: integration tests that simulate mixed CUTLASS/Triton versions and exercise dlopen permutations (owner: Ben Carter)
- Rollout automation: per-host feature flag and canary group config (owner: Platform Automation)

Testing and rollout plan:
1) Unit tests for loader abstraction and negative tests for RTLD_LOCAL behavior. 2) CI matrix: (CUDA 12.6/13.0) x (Triton 2.x/3.x) x (cutlass variants) with both dlmopen and RTLD_LOCAL paths. 3) Internal dogfood fleet rollout to non-critical clusters for 72h. 4) External canary (5% of capacity) for 48h with automated rollback if crash rate >0.5% or latency regression detected. 5) Gradual ramp to 100% over 2 weeks.

Monitoring and observability:
- New telemetry events: loader.mode, namespace.created, symbol-collision-warn, kernel.bound -> send to runtime-tracing and cost/latency dashboards.
- Add Grafana panel: symbol-collision-count and per-host loader-mode. Create alert: symbol-collision-count > 1 in 15m for canary group.

Risks and mitigations:
- Some vendor libraries require global symbols: provide legacy-global opt-in and a signing/whitelist flow. - Performance overhead from indirection: measure method call overhead and avoid introducing per-token path work; audit hotpaths and JIT inliner hints. - Platform portability: dlmopen not available on older distros; fallback to RTLD_LOCAL and additional shim logic.

Alternatives considered:
- Static symbol renaming at build time (ABI renaming). Rejected because many third-party closed-source binaries cannot be rebuilt. - Containerizing each model into its own PID/namespace to guarantee isolation. Too heavy operationally and increases memory usage.

Deliverables:
- runtime/loader: namespace support + config toggle (PR, tests) - runtime-1.24 release
- installer: symbol scanner and warnings
- telemetry: kernel-binding events and Grafana dashboard
- CI job: mixed-version compatibility suite

Notes on scope and follow-ups: This ticket focuses on runtime loader and immediate compatibility tooling. Follow-up tickets will cover automated symbol remediation (binary patch suggestions), signing UX for overrides, and retrospective audits for historical bundles.
